concepts.def: The Sun, eight planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
Planets orbit the Sun in ellipses.
Gravity provides the centripetal force for orbits.
Icy bodies on highly elliptical orbits.
Rocky bodies, mostly between Mars and Jupiter.
Bodies like Pluto that don't clear their orbit.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Solar System Dynamics — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Solar System Dynamics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Solar System Dynamics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Length of the solar cycle (sunspot count)?
options: 1 year
11 years
22 years
50 years

mcqs.q: Charged particles streaming from the Sun are called?
options: Solar flares
Solar wind
Aurora
Cosmic rays

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter classified as a gas giant?
options: Its bulk is mostly hydrogen and helium with no defined solid surface.
It is mostly air like Earth's atmosphere.
It is made of fire.
Comets are larger than asteroids.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an asteroid and a comet?
options: It is the hottest stage.
Asteroids are rocky/metallic; comets contain ice that vaporises near the Sun, producing a tail.
They are the same object with different names.
Comets are larger than asteroids.

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It is the hottest stage.
It is the largest stage of a star's life.
It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
It is made of fire.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Coronal mass ejection”?
options: Glows from atmospheric atoms excited by solar particles channelled along Earth's field lines.
Continuous stream of charged particles flowing from the Sun's corona at 400-800 km/s.
Sudden intense burst of X-ray and UV radiation from magnetic reconnection above sunspots.
Huge eruption of plasma and magnetic field into space; can cause geomagnetic storms.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Solar flare”?
options: Sudden intense burst of X-ray and UV radiation from magnetic reconnection above sunspots.
Huge eruption of plasma and magnetic field into space; can cause geomagnetic storms.
Glows from atmospheric atoms excited by solar particles channelled along Earth's field lines.
~11-year cycle of sunspot number and magnetic activity; full magnetic cycle is 22 years.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Solar wind”?
options: Glows from atmospheric atoms excited by solar particles channelled along Earth's field lines.
Sudden intense burst of X-ray and UV radiation from magnetic reconnection above sunspots.
Cooler regions (~3,800 K) on the photosphere with strong magnetic fields (~0.3 T).
Continuous stream of charged particles flowing from the Sun's corona at 400-800 km/s.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Solar cycle”?
options: Glows from atmospheric atoms excited by solar particles channelled along Earth's field lines.
Huge eruption of plasma and magnetic field into space; can cause geomagnetic storms.
~11-year cycle of sunspot number and magnetic activity; full magnetic cycle is 22 years.
Continuous stream of charged particles flowing from the Sun's corona at 400-800 km/s.
